subject: Post-call: Long-context evals / truncation behavior / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Bob Jones <bob.jones@acme.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Long-context evals / truncation behavior / next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Bob — really helpful to understand the Acme summarization + search use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

What we heard
- Large legal/policy documents (~20–200k tokens) are the primary input.
- Key requirements: high-fidelity summarization (no hallucinated facts), consistent extraction of clause-level metadata, and predictable truncation behavior when context exceeds model window.
- Production constraints: sub-1s token latency not required; throughput of ~100 concurrent requests during peak; data residency in US.

Redwood recommendation (initial)
- Run parallel evals on two model profiles: redwood-chat-13b (strong instruction-following, cheaper) and redwood-llama-70b-q8 (higher fidelity on long-context / summarization). If 70b latency/cost is prohibitive, test open-llama-30b-quant as a middle ground.
- Use quantized variants for Dedicated/private deployment to save cost.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) You share representative sample docs (you mentioned 5–10 docs); attach as ZIP.
2) We run a long-context eval (see attached plan) that tests: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity, and extraction accuracy. Plan includes random windowing, full-document summarization, and pseudo-streaming tests.
3) Marcus (cc'd) will run a quick compatibility check on your files + estimate tokens/cost.
4) We deliver results and a recommended model/profile + prompt set within ~7 business days after receiving samples.

Attachments: redwood-long-context-eval-plan.pdf (evaluation matrix + prompt sets), sample-cost-estimate.csv

If that works, send the sample docs and any compliance notes (NDA/PO), and we'll kick off the eval.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Bob — appreciate the sample ZIP, got it. Answers inline and attaching our eval plan PDF for your review.

Pricing (ballpark for eval runs)
- redwood-chat-13b (quant): ~$30–$60 for a full-suite eval across 6 docs (depends on tokenization / context expansion).
- redwood-llama-70b-q8: ~$400–$700 for the same eval (higher per-token).
We can run a lightweight smoke test first (one doc) to validate instrumentation before the full suite to reduce initial cost.

Truncation detection
- We instrument the runtime to expose a truncation flag when inputs exceed the window and content is dropped prior to generation. For streaming/segmented summary flows we also provide start/end token indices and a confidence score. We will include these in the eval outputs so you can assert on them.

Prompt sets and evaluation rubric
- Attached in the eval plan: canonical prompts for full-document summarization, rolling-window summarization, and clause extraction. We also include automated metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) and manual spot-check criteria for hallucination and fidelity.

Quality regression concerns
- We recommend running the eval against both the current version and a canary model variant. Redwood’s rollout tooling lets you compare outputs and automatically revert a rollout if regression thresholds (e.g., >5% drop in extraction F1 or significant hallucination cases) are exceeded.

Attachment: redwood-long-context-eval-plan.pdf

Marcus and Rishi — can one of you pick up the token/cost estimate and a quick test plan for ingesting the ZIP?

Best,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Long-context evals / truncation behavior / next steps

Hey Bob — I pulled the ZIP and did a quick pass. A few technical notes and next steps: 

1) Tokenization estimate
- The 6 docs average ~85k tokens raw. For a rolling-window eval (2k window with 1k stride) expect ~170k input tokens across the suite; full-document runs (if supported) are ~510k tokens when we include system prompt + instruction overhead.

2) Truncation behavior / indicators
- Confirming Marissa: our runtime will return a metadata field "context_truncated": true/false and a "truncation_point_token_index" when truncation occurs. We can also provide per-chunk confidence scores.

3) Proposed pilot (low cost)
- Run smoke test on 1 doc on both redwood-chat-13b and redwood-llama-70b-q8 (quant). Produce: full-doc summary, rolling-window summaries (2k windows), and clause extraction output.
- Deliverables: raw outputs, automated metric table, 10 manual spot-checks highlighting hallucination/fidelity.

4) Shared artifacts
- I uploaded a short compatibility report and a token/cost worksheet to our shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqExampleSharedDriveLink

If you approve the pilot, we'll schedule the smoke run tomorrow and follow with the full-suite within 5 business days.

—Marcus
